subject: Future Tech
title: What Is CRISPR?
description: A 60-second lesson on What Is CRISPR?.

hook.text: CRISPR stands for Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats.

buildup.text: When a virus attacks, bacteria capture a snippet of its DNA and store it.

discovery.text: Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier realized this system could be reprogrammed to cut any DNA sequence at will.

twist.text: CRISPR-Cas9 uses a guide RNA to find the target and a Cas9 protein to cut it. It's like GPS plus molecular scissors.

climax.text: Their 2012 paper launched a revolution. Within months, labs worldwide were editing genes in human cells and organisms.

punchline.text: Bacteria invented gene editing. Humans borrowed it.

quiz.question: Who adapted CRISPR for gene editing in 2012?
